ArchitectureDriftData.description:
v0.4.0 I3.1 - spec §10. Deliberately only the service and the drift claim ids: no
`observed_only[]`/`not_observed[]` buckets, no `severity`/`score`/`summary_text` (spec §10 names
each of those as prohibited), because every returned `DependencyClaim` already carries the
authoritative `qualification` that made it drift. The claims themselves stay on the enclosing
`ArchitectureAnswer.claims` - this data payload only names them, in the same order.
ArchitectureDriftData.title: ArchitectureDriftData

CandidateEntry.description: One evaluated v2 candidate: its I2 summary and **every** admitted pair (D4, D10).
CandidateEntry.title: CandidateEntry

CandidateLimitationCode.description: The internal I2 limitation codes (D4, D13.4, D14.1), carried unchanged.
CandidateLimitationCode.title: CandidateLimitationCode

CapturedWorkloadKind.description: I2 D14.1: the captured Kubernetes kind exactly.
CapturedWorkloadKind.title: CapturedWorkloadKind

CapturedWorkloadRef.description:
The I2 `CapturedWorkload` as resolved by one pair or candidate. `uid` is null only when the
capture carried none (`WORKLOAD_UID_UNAVAILABLE`, I2 D14.1).
CapturedWorkloadRef.title: CapturedWorkloadRef

ComparedMembership.description:
A `(provider Service or unresolved owner, Operation)` membership positive in one scope.
`provider_service_id` is null when the owner is unresolved (D8).
ComparedMembership.title: ComparedMembership

Comparison.description:
D10 comparison of two selected scopes. Labels mean "positively evidenced here", never
"absent there".
Comparison.title: Comparison

Completeness.description: Relative to the evaluated inventory only (I3 §7, §9); never "the system was observed".
Completeness.title: Completeness

DeploymentClaim.description:
I3 spec §12: the public `Service -[DEPLOYED_AS]-> Workload` claim. Deliberately has no
`delivery`/`qualification`/`coverage`/`destination_resolution` fields - those are
`DependencyClaim`-only concepts describing a CALLS/SENDS interaction, and `DEPLOYED_AS` is never
an interaction (spec §1: "DEPLOYED_AS != CALLS != SENDS != RECEIVES_FROM").
DeploymentClaim.title: DeploymentClaim

DeploymentResolution.description:
I3 spec §13.3: the public resolution-outcome shape, returned for every reconciliation
candidate group whether it produced a claim or not - "Resolved and non-resolved outcomes SHALL
be inspectable without fabricating a claim."
DeploymentResolution.title: DeploymentResolution

DeploymentResolutionMethod.description:
I3 spec §10.1: only the three *successful* identity-path outcomes - never CONFLICT/
AMBIGUOUS/UNRESOLVED, which are never a "method" a claim can be supported by. Compare
`DeploymentResolutionStatus` below, which is the wider 6-value outcome set a
`DeploymentResolution` (as opposed to an actual `DeploymentClaim`) may carry.
DeploymentResolutionMethod.title: DeploymentResolutionMethod

DeploymentResolutionStatus.description:
I3 spec §13.3: the wider 6-value outcome set a `DeploymentResolution` may carry - the three
successful `DeploymentResolutionMethod` values plus the three non-resolved outcomes. Kept as its
own enum (not reusing `DeploymentResolutionMethod`) since CONFLICT/AMBIGUOUS/UNRESOLVED are never
valid `DeploymentClaim.resolution_method`/`.supporting_methods` values (spec §10.1: "Similarity is
never a successful path" - and conflict/ambiguity are never "methods" either).
DeploymentResolutionStatus.title: DeploymentResolutionStatus

EvaluatedSource.description: A capture source that formed at least one pair (D10 `evaluated_sources`).
EvaluatedSource.title: EvaluatedSource

EvidenceData.description:
v0.4.0 I2.1 - spec §11.2/§12. `claims`/top-level `evidence_refs` on the enclosing
`ArchitectureAnswer` stay empty for this tool - lookup creates no claim; resolved ids live here.
EvidenceData.title: EvidenceData

EvidenceEntry.description: One requested ref (D11). A `NOT_FOUND` entry never says why.
EvidenceEntry.title: EvidenceEntry

EvidenceRecord.description:
v0.4.0 I2.1 - spec §11.2. `evidence_type`/`source_type` reuse the existing
`app.provenance.model` enums rather than redefining them - no new adapter classification.
EvidenceRecord.title: EvidenceRecord

EvidenceRefKind.description: D11: what a resolved ref is.
EvidenceRefKind.title: EvidenceRefKind

EvidenceRelationType.description:
v0.4.0 I2.1 - the closed set of canonical graph relation kinds (spec §11.2's `supports`),
widened by I3 (DEPLOYED_AS) and v0.5.0 I4 (PUBLISHES_TO/SUBSCRIPTION_OF). Deliberately its own
closed enum rather than reusing `DeliveryRelationType` (only the delivery relations) or a
graph-layer string - `get_evidence` describes existing facts, never a new architecture claim.
EvidenceRelationType.title: EvidenceRelationType

EvidenceRequest.description:
v0.4.0 I2.1 - the `get_evidence` request shape (spec §11.1). Unlike
`ServiceDependenciesRequest`, `snapshot_id` is required here - `get_evidence` never defaults to
the current snapshot, and there is no observation-context input at all.
EvidenceRequest.title: EvidenceRequest

IngestionResult.description: I1 spec §10: "Each source receives exactly one result."
IngestionResult.title: IngestionResult

InventoryBounds.description: The D4 values actually applied to this answer page.
InventoryBounds.title: InventoryBounds

LocalDisposition.description: I1 §10 / I2 dispositions, carried unchanged inside the payload (never envelope outcomes).
LocalDisposition.title: LocalDisposition

LocalQualification.description: I2 D14.4: every assertion has v2, so only these two are reachable.
LocalQualification.title: LocalQualification

LocalityAnswer.description:
The 0.6 envelope (D2, D9). `data` is null exactly for a refusal that evaluated nothing; an
evaluated `NOT_ANSWERED` still carries its inventory or entries.
LocalityAnswer.title: LocalityAnswer

LocalityLimitation.description: `reasons` carries the I2 `LOCALITY_*` codes behind the limitation, if any.
LocalityLimitation.title: LocalityLimitation

LocalityLimitationCode.description: D9: the closed 0.6 envelope codes, separate from the 0.5 `LimitationCode`.
LocalityLimitationCode.title: LocalityLimitationCode

LocalityRequestContext.description:
The normalized, evaluated request (D3, D10). An evaluated request is supported, so its
relation, dimensions and days are the supported forms.
LocalityRequestContext.title: LocalityRequestContext

LocalityWorkload.description: A positive caller Workload: its exact identity plus presentation-only name/logical id.
LocalityWorkload.title: LocalityWorkload

ObservedEvidenceMetadata.description:
v0.4.0 I2.1 - spec §11.2: bounded observed-evidence metadata only. No raw payloads,
authorization values, full spans, baggage, resource attributes, or sample trace ids.
ObservedEvidenceMetadata.title: ObservedEvidenceMetadata

OperationAssessment.description:
One I2 `QualifiedLocalEvidenceAssessment`, values unchanged. The subject, relation,
environment, window, caller Workload and snapshot are carried once by the containing locality,
request context and envelope (D16.3).
OperationAssessment.title: OperationAssessment

PairEntry.description:
One admitted (candidate, source) pair, unchanged from I2 (D13). Only an `APPLICABLE` pair
carries a resolved Workload (`_phase_4`).
PairEntry.title: PairEntry

ProviderGroup.description: D8: one provider Service in one caller Workload. No group-level qualification.
ProviderGroup.title: ProviderGroup

ProviderOwnerReason.description: D8: zero or several evidenced `PROVIDES` owners.
ProviderOwnerReason.title: ProviderOwnerReason

ReportEffectSet.description:
One category of canonical effects, by stable identity. Public canonical facts are listed
(node ids and `TYPE:source:target` relation keys); internal-only facts (Kubernetes
infrastructure, Pub/Sub carriers, Evidence) are only counted, because I2 §9 keeps them out of
every public payload.
ReportEffectSet.title: ReportEffectSet

ReportEffects.description:
The canonical committed effects of one source's reconciliation (I1 §10), from its claim
reconciliation plan: claims it newly owns (`added`), retained claims it changed (`changed`),
dropped claims no other source will own after the run (`expired`), and dropped claims that
survive for another owner (`ownership_removed`). Each set is attributed to this source alone
and does not depend on the order in which the run's sources are reconciled. An unchanged
replay has four empty sets and does not advance the graph revision. Null in a run that did not
commit: such a run changes nothing (I1 §6).
ReportEffects.title: ReportEffects

ReportEmittedCounts.description: What the source's adapter mapped, before reconciliation (I1 §10 "emitted counts").
ReportEmittedCounts.title: ReportEmittedCounts

ReportRemoval.description:
One previously committed source removed by an authorized removal, with its effects (only
`expired` and `ownership_removed` can be non-empty).
ReportRemoval.title: ReportRemoval

ScopeEvaluation.description: D10: a selected identity's status, derived only from the evaluated inventory.
ScopeEvaluation.title: ScopeEvaluation

ScopedV2Record.description: D11: the admitted public fields of one `ScopedObservedCallV2` (v2 contract §1, §3).
ScopedV2Record.title: ScopedV2Record

ServiceDependenciesData.description:
v0.5.0 I3 spec §14.2: deployment is a separate sibling projection, never a dependency -
`deployment_claim_ids`/`deployment_resolutions` are additive fields alongside the original
dependency-only shape, not a replacement of it.
ServiceDependenciesData.title: ServiceDependenciesData

ServiceDeploymentsView.description:
v0.5.0 I3 spec §15: the REST-only projection `GET /{service_id}/deployments` returns - not a
public MCP contract type (there is no matching MCP tool for this view), so it lives here rather
than in `contracts.py`. Every field is extracted from one already-computed
`get_service_dependencies` answer (spec §15: "MUST NOT invoke deployment reconciliation, Neo4j
queries, or qualification logic independently") - this model has no validators of its own beyond
shape, since the answer it projects is already fully validated.
ServiceDeploymentsView.title: ServiceDeploymentsView

SourceLimitation.description: A non-applicable pair of a contributing candidate (I2 `source_limitations`).
SourceLimitation.title: SourceLimitation

SupportedFact.description:
v0.4.0 I2.1 - spec §11.2: one existing canonical relation fact an evidence record supports.
Not a generic graph record and not a new architecture claim - only the 3 bounded fields.
SupportedFact.title: SupportedFact

WorkloadIdentity.description:
D3: an exact captured caller Workload. The captured UID is required; `name` is never part of
the identity.
WorkloadIdentity.title: WorkloadIdentity

WorkloadKind.description:
I3 spec §8.1: the exact supported Kubernetes controller kinds a deployment identity path may
resolve to - the same closed set I2's own owner-chain resolution already admits.
WorkloadKind.title: WorkloadKind

WorkloadRef.description:
I3 spec §11: a bounded public Workload reference, deliberately its own model rather than an
`EntityRef` extension. `EntityRef` is reused by `DependencyClaim.subject`/`.object` and
`DeliveryRef.via` - widening its type-specific-field validator with a WORKLOAD branch would make
a Workload-shaped `EntityRef` constructible inside a dependency claim, exactly the governing
"DEPLOYED_AS != CALLS" / entity-equivalence boundary spec §1 forbids. `DeploymentClaim.object` is
typed `WorkloadRef`, never `EntityRef`, for the same reason.

Cluster UID, Pod UID, source inventory, resource UID, and owner-chain details remain evidence
drill-down, not fields of this relation target (spec §11's own rule) - `namespace` here is
identity context, not a locality qualification.
WorkloadRef.title: WorkloadRef

O4 (spec §45/§47). status is always the literal NOT_OBSERVED_IN_WINDOW (H4.16).
O3 (spec §44/§47/§48 - the one literal example response this endpoint's shape follows).

`POST /api/evidence/resolve` (spec §14.5): calls
`ArchitectureIntelligenceService.get_evidence` exactly once and returns its answer unchanged.

schema.title: Response Get Evidence Api Evidence  Evidence Id  Get

post.description:
POST /api/import - imports every configured source (I1 spec §14). Each configured
directory is its own atomic discovery run (I1 spec §6): one run's PARTIAL/FAILED status never
blocks another's commit. The response is the versioned I1 §10 import report
(`app.ingestion.import_report`).

POST /api/import/service/{serviceId} reimports every configured source and reports the
resulting stats, then confirms the requested canonical Service ID (e.g. "service:order-
service") now exists. Under I1, a service may be declared by more than one source and a source
may declare more than one service (ADR 0009), so a single-source-scoped reimport is no longer
a meaningful unit - the whole configured scope is always reimported.

Response Get Message Api Messages  Message Id  Get

post.description:
POST /api/query: a known-intent question is answered by an existing deterministic analysis
(spec §6); only an unrecognized question falls back to validated read-only LLM-generated
Cypher (spec §14/§15).

`GET /api/services/{service_id}/deployments` (spec §15). Unlike `/dependencies`/`/drift`,

missing one for free), and an `UNKNOWN_ENTITY` limitation becomes a real 404 - the one spec-frozen
exception to this file's "everything else stays 200" rule (see the module docstring).
Evidence backing every relation incident to this service (spec §4.10, AC13).

post.description:
OTLP/HTTP trace ingestion (spec §8): decode -> resolve against declared data -> persist
observed facts/evidence (spec §36, Iteration 11E). Content-type/decode validation happens
before any Neo4j access, so a malformed request never touches the graph.
